entities.name: PMID:27520023
observations: Herrmann et al. studied pedunculate oak microcuttings with alternating endogenous shoot and root growth flushes during interaction with Pratylenchus penetrans, with or without Piloderma croceum; systemic responses were measured by leaf transcriptomics.

Without Piloderma, P. penetrans elicited about 16-fold more differentially expressed genes during shoot flush than root flush, with phase-dependent defense, hormone, ROS, lipid-signaling, and metabolism responses.

With Piloderma, the phase-specific pattern shifted toward stronger P. penetrans effects during root flush, indicating that endogenous rhythmic growth modulated the interaction-associated host response.

The evidence directly supports a strong growth-stage effect on host transcriptomic responses, but the retrieved study description does not establish a large change in nematode burden, reproduction, or population growth.

entities.name: Quercus robur
observations: Pedunculate oak used as the host plant in the transcriptomic study of endogenous rhythmic growth and Pratylenchus penetrans interaction.

entities.name: Pratylenchus penetrans
observations: Migratory plant-parasitic nematode used to challenge Quercus robur roots.

entities.name: Rhythmic growth transcriptomic effect
observations: In Quercus robur, endogenous shoot/root growth phase strongly changed systemic leaf transcriptomic responses to Pratylenchus penetrans; the contrast was approximately 16-fold in the number of differentially expressed genes without Piloderma croceum.
This finding concerns host molecular interaction responses; direct nematode fitness effects were not reported in the retrieved abstract-level evidence.
